minutes.headline: Assessors set the FY26 overlay request at $175,000 by unanimous vote and adopted a deed-discrepancy letter policy.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard the principal assessor's status report (abatements, motor vehicle excise abatements, cyclical inspections by Vision Appraisal, Chapter land applications). It adopted a deed letter policy, approved minutes and released executive-session minutes, signed motor vehicle abatement groups, voted an overlay request, and discussed the senior means-tested exemption and the tax billing/MUNIS responsibility dispute. It ended by entering executive session on abatement and exemption applications.

budget_items.what_was_said: Principal assessor reported real estate and personal property abatement counts and amount granted to date.

Maximum exemption would follow the circuit breaker amount; capped at 1% of the levy, with burden shifting to other taxpayers; asset limit discussed.

HERO Act motor vehicle abatements must be issued as physical abatements, not removed from the commitment; the process should be documented.
Senior exemption application deadline targeted as the first Wednesday in September.
Principal assessor to try to arrange a joint meeting with the DOR attorney, the board, the finance director and town manager on the tax billing responsibility question.
Overlay request to be communicated to the finance director by email.
Meetings set for March 19, April 2 and April 16.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted to set the FY26 overlay request, the amount as heard, after reviewing overlay balances and abatement history.
The board voted to accept a deed-discrepancy letter as its policy and proceed with it.
The board agreed to try for a joint meeting with the DOR attorney, the finance director and the town manager on who is responsible for tax billing.
The board approved Chapter land status for about 8.9 acres on Island Road and voted to release two sets of executive session minutes.
The board discussed a senior means-tested exemption, targeting a first-Wednesday-in-September application deadline; no vote was taken.

why_it_matters: The overlay is the reserve the town sets aside from the tax levy to cover abatements, so the amount voted feeds into how much the tax rate has to raise.
A senior means-tested exemption is capped at 1% of the levy, so its cost would shift to other taxpayers, and a warrant article for it may reach Town Meeting voters.
The unresolved question of who is responsible for tax billing and MUNIS affects who produces and corrects resident tax bills.
